newsitem.title: Australia: Australia Yield Spreads - Widen sharply vs the bloc.
newsitem.headline: Australia Yield Spreads - Widen sharply vs the bloc.

text.p: Australian bond yields blew out sharply against the dollar bloc after the outcome of the March quarter inflation report, which, while weak, was not as benign as the market had been hoping for in the past few days.

However, the data still showed headline annual inflation at its lowest level for four years at 1.3 percent and the policy sensitive underlying rate remaining at the low end of the Reserve Bank 2.0-3.0 percent target at 2.1 percent.

The data follows hot-on-the-heels of Tuesday's moderate A$10 per week award to low paid workers by the Australian Industrial Relations Commission, which is seen keeping annual average weekly earnings within the RBA's 4.0-4.5 percent comfort zone.
These outcomes, along with other data showing a patchy recovery, should help to underpin the bond market.

"While I am still negative on bonds long term, we're in a great little patch at the moment," said Matthew Drennan, senior economist at Axiom Funds Management, adding that spreads to the U.S. will likely tighten again.

"In the short term, it is inevitable because they are still in a tightening cycle over there (in the U.S.). But I regard it as a bubble though, and I don't think it is sustainable below 100 basis points," he added.
He, and other analysts, feel that Australia will ultimately follow the U.S. cycle and the 10-year spread will blow out to more sustainable levels in the 100-130 basis point range.

The market had put in a strong outperformance against the bloc before the data with the Australian/U.S. 10-year bond yield spread having got close to last week's low of around 90 basis points at one stage.
